text:
sophia: heads up — saw a sharp bump in provisional token hits during the 09:04 canary swap. lots of sessions show provisional > confirmed after a toolcall got truncated midstream. attaching minimal repro and logs

kevin: can you paste the repro and a log sample? is this reproducing locally or only in canary? @kevin

sophia: repro (curl):
```bash
curl -s -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"open-variant-3b","stream":true,"input":"<long prompt>"}' \n  https://api.redwood.example/v2/generate?route=router-v2
```
observed log snippet (router) — truncated for brevity:
```
[09:04:12] request_id=req_0a1b2 route=router-v2 -> shard-a: allocated session s-123
[09:04:18] model_swap start: open-variant-3b -> opt-quant-3b at 10%
[09:04:21] s-123 toolcall:start token_streaming
[09:04:22] s-123 toolcall:truncated by router (fallback to smaller model) -> session closed; provisional_tokens=142; confirmed_tokens=0
```

jamie: yep i've seen this pattern. when a midstream model swap triggers a fallback we currently mark tokens provisional until the session finalizes. if a toolcall truncates and router closes the session early, finalization never happens and provisional stays provisional (and shows up as a spike).

maya: that explains the console blip. UX-wise we should surface a "tentative" column alongside "provisional" so PMs can filter sessions that never finalized. also we need a telemetry metric for finalization lag so we can alert when provisional backlog grows.

kevin: two related questions: 1) should the internal router API expose an explicit finalize/confirm call to the ledger? 2) can we rely on client-sent confirm headers? both have replay/idempotency pitfalls.

sophia: 1) I think router->ledger confirm is safest; server-side has ownership over whether the session completed successfully. 2) client confirms are risky — retries could double-confirm unless we have strong monotonic session ids + dedupe.

jamie: proposal: add a lightweight ack endpoint in routing (POST /internal/session/{id}/confirm) that accepts {confirm:true, final_tokens: N} and is idempotent based on session_id+seq. router invokes it when it knows the session ended cleanly. if session closed due to truncation, router can send confirm=false + reason=truncation so ledger can mark and issue provisional accounting treatment.

kevin: sounds reasonable. need to define the idempotency key. we already have session_id and last_seq_seen — use (session_id, last_seq) pair. also add a guard: if confirm=true but ledger already has confirmed tokens for that (session_id,last_seq) pair, ignore.

maya: for the console change, I'll mock a small wireframe. telemetry query we'd want to add (in psql):
```sql
SELECT session_id, route, provisional_tokens, confirmed_tokens, closed_reason, finalized_at
FROM session_accounting
WHERE created_at > now() - interval '24 hours'
  AND provisional_tokens > 0
ORDER BY provisional_tokens DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
That helps populate the tentative/provisional dashboard tile.

deploy-bot: deploy: canary router-v2 -> 10% (09:04) :rocket:

infra-bot: FYI — I flagged routes with >30% provisional-to-confirmed ratio in the last hour. alert created: AGENT-2982.

kevin: followups:
- (infra) instrument session_finalization_lag_ms and provisional_to_confirmed_ratio per-route
- (eng-router) add internal confirm endpoint + idempotency keys (PR + tests)
- (devex/maya) console tile showing tentative/provisional and link to sample session ids
- (pm) decide policy for auto-finalize after Xs of inactivity (probably 24h)

sophia: will open the router issue and drop logs+repro in it. assigning to kevin/jamie for design/impl. thanks.

jamie: +1, will sketch idempotency behavior. :thumbsup:

maya: I'll add the dashboard ticket and attach that SQL as a starting point.

kevin: adding notes: be careful with toolcall semantics — some toolcalls intentionally truncate but still produce meaningful confirmed tokens (we need the confirm=false reason to preserve semantics).

sophia: good catch. we'll include reason enum: {completed, truncated_by_router, client_eof, error}.

jamie: ok moving to create PR for router confirm endpoint tomorrow AM.

sophia: thanks all — tagging @kevin @maya for visibility.
